title: Settings Update Field
prompt: A React settings form stores values in one object. Write a helper that returns a new form object with the requested field updated.

explanation.beginner:
Example: settingsUpdateField({"name":"Ada","email":""}, "email", "ada@example.com") produces {"name":"Ada","email":"ada@example.com"}. Choose the targeted field or record, create its new state, and preserve unaffected values from the previous state.

Compare “adds new fields”: input [{"name":"Ada"},"role","admin"] produces {"name":"Ada","role":"admin"}. Explain which rule causes the difference before writing code.
explanation.junior:
Choose the targeted field or record, create its new state, and preserve unaffected values from the previous state.

Tempting mistake: Mutating the previous state can corrupt undo and comparisons. Copying only the outer collection still shares nested objects.

Trace the branch conditions and any accumulator or lookup after each input. Keep the return contract separate from how it is calculated.

Regression check: preserve the contract illustrated by “adds new fields”, then change one boundary in a new test. The solution below is one implementation; another is valid when it preserves the same behavior.
